links.outcome: Validity of references cited by ChatGPT in answers about radiopharmaceutical extravasation
links.effect: One physician's reference check found no hallucinations. Fully validated references were used for 11 of 15 questions and general medical and ethical guidelines for 4 questions.
links.quote: The reference check revealed no AI hallucinations.

links.outcome: Inconsistency of ChatGPT responses across three repeated queries per question
links.effect: Irrelevant or minor inconsistencies in 87% of questions; some differences relevant to main content in the other 13%.
links.quote: The evaluators also rated the inconsistency across the three ChatGPT responses for each question and found irrelevant or minor inconsistencies in 87% of questions and some differences relevant to main content in the other 13% of the questions.

unlisted_practices: Comparing chatbot patient-counseling answers with official professional society positions and staff communications

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT's performance in answering patient questions regarding radiopharmaceutical extravasations, rated by clinical experts.
